newsitem.title: USA: Fed seen refraining from intervention on Friday.
newsitem.headline: Fed seen refraining from intervention on Friday.

text.p: The Federal Reserve was seen not likely to intervene at its usual midmorning period on Friday, economists said.

"The total of $6.4 billion added Thursday by the first tranche of the Fed's coupon pass and a seven-day fixed-term repurchase agreement falls a bit shy of the weekend add need -- thus we could not rule out a small (less than $2 billion) RP to fill the gap," said Marc Wanshel, economist with Morgan Guaranty Trust Co. "More likely, however, the funds rate will be held down by the usual Friday fade and the Fed will refrain from market action."
Fed funds were trading at the Fed's current official target level of 5-1/2 percent.
